LESSON: TARAWEEH AND WITR

Grade: Grade 5
Subject: ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
Strand: Devotional Acts
Topic 4.2.2: Taraweeh and Witr

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Taraweeh and Witr. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: how they perform Taraweeh/witr prayers. What is the significance of performing swalatul Taraweeh and witr?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. perform swalatul Taraweeh and witr for spiritual nourishment
2. appreciate the performance of Taraweeh and witr prayers to earn thawab

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: TARAWEEH AND WITR
Subject: ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION · Grade: Grade 5
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Taraweeh and Witr helps you succeed in ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

KEY FACTS: TARAWEEH AND WITR
Study Taraweeh and Witr like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Perform swalatul Taraweeh and witr for spiritual nourishment

What this means
In this part you learn to perform swalatul Taraweeh and witr for spiritual nourishment. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: perform swalatul Taraweeh and witr for spiritual nourishment.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Taraweeh and Witr” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can perform swalatul Taraweeh and witr for spiritual nourishment. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Appreciate the performance of Taraweeh and witr prayers to earn thawab

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate the performance of Taraweeh and witr prayers to earn thawab. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate the performance of Taraweeh and witr prayers to earn thawab.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Story link: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Taraweeh and Witr in your own words.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate the performance of Taraweeh and witr prayers to earn thawab. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Taraweeh and Witr is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Show how “Taraweeh and Witr” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: perform swalatul Taraweeh and witr for spiritual nourishment)

Example 2: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Taraweeh and Witr in your own words. (skill: appreciate the performance of Taraweeh and witr prayers to earn thawab)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Taraweeh and Witr to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: perform swalatul Taraweeh and witr for spiritual nourishment.
3. Practise this skill: appreciate the performance of Taraweeh and witr prayers to earn thawab.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Taraweeh and Witr from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Taraweeh and Witr: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 5 learner study Taraweeh and Witr?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. how they perform Taraweeh/witr prayers. What is the significance of performing swalatul Taraweeh and witr?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Taraweeh and Witr means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: perform swalatul Taraweeh and witr for spiritual nourishment.
5. Be able to: appreciate the performance of Taraweeh and witr prayers to earn thawab.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
